author: IGN
description:
Finally, Rockstar is making huge changes to its signature gameplay mechanic: stealing cars. From a tiered vehicle security system to the varied set of tools you’ll be using to steal them with, and new ways to profit directly from each theft, Rockstar’s latest is looking to change the game we’ve all been used to in some big ways. A humble hotwire won’t cut it anymore; instead, you’ll be expected to pay a bit more attention, with some cars being harder to crack than others! 

Expect trackers that reveal your location to the police, citizens reporting your ride as stolen, and buyers looking to take those stolen cars off your hands. All of this and more adds to GTA 6’s level of enhanced simulation. Will this more organic approach to moment-to-moment gameplay pay off? Stick around, as we break down this fundamental yet exciting change.

#IGN #Gaming #GTA6
title: GTA 6 Changes How You Steal Cars - Rockstar Explains

author: IGN
description:
During a recent hands-off demo of GTA 6 at Rockstar HQ, we spotted the quiet return of something that hasn’t been a major part of the series for over twenty years. But we’re not talking about big perms and leg warmers, we’re talking about body building.

Before the dizzying realism of Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA San Andreas was undoubtedly Rockstar’s most ambitious game: a deep world simulation with an array of RPG stats and character customisation options that had an impact on the gameplay and were noticed by the game’s reactive NPCs. The system was well ahead of its time, though many players bounced off it. Often on the grounds that watching your diet and going to the gym in real life isn’t fun, so it shouldn’t be a mandatory minigame in an escapist fantasy.

Well, Rockstar have decided to bring it all back for GTA 6: you can take Jason and Lucia to the gym, alone or together, to work on their lats and six-packs. And, yes, you can overeat to make them fat, which might not be great fo
title: In GTA 6 San Andreas' RPG Stats Are Back - Rockstar Explains

author: IGN
description:
Think you know how to escape the cops in GTA? Think again: GTA 6’s expanded wanted system is a tense game of cat and mouse.

During our hands-off GTA 6 demo with Rockstar, studio co-head Rob Nelson took some time to detail the new wanted system. There’s still your basic six star levels of police aggression, but GTA 6’s sophisticated new chase and surveillance mechanics make a much more granular system than before, with police now taking into account CCTV footage as well as witness phone calls to close in on you. But you also have more ways to evade them. Individual items of clothing are now taken into account, alongside the vehicle you’re driving, the severity of the crime, and even the company you keep.

#IGN #Gaming #GTA6
title: In GTA 6 You're Not Just Wanted, You're Hunted - Rockstar Explains

author: IGN
description:
Lucia and Jason's relationship is central to the narrative, but in GTA 6, engaging with the mechanics of this dynamic partnership seems to be optional in every way that matters. It's not just a crime of life you'll be able to share as Jason or Lucia, but the small things too, whether you're shopping, holding hands, texting one another, playing pool, or even kayaking; don't worry, though, you can still rob stores, banks, and more, and all of the above have a positive impact on their relationship. Rockstar has written a couple that works on many levels, and we'll break down how this felony inclined relationship will play out!

#IGN #Gaming #GTA6
title: GTA 6: Rockstar Is Ready To Prove It Can Do Romance

Obviously game design has moved on since then, so we sat down with Miles Tost, Level Design Lead and the legendary voice of Geralt himself Doug Cockle, to go over the challenges in returning to The Witcher 3 after so long. 

We also got to mine some details from them both about the Remaster, asking our burning questions on changes to combat and skill progression.
